title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement: You get a list of numbers and a width k. A window of width k slides from the left end to the right end, one step at a time. For every position of the window, report the largest number inside it.

example.caption: The first window [1, 3, -1] has maximum 3. Sliding right gives 3, 5, 5, 6 and 7 for the others.

idea.sentence: Keep a queue of candidate positions whose values fall from front to back. A new number removes every weaker one behind it, so the front is always the window's maximum.

jargon.plain: A queue you can add to and remove from at both ends.
Always going one way. Here the values in the deque only ever fall from front to back.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the list, then k, e.g. [1,3,1,2,0,5], 3

compare.bruteLabel: Scan every window for its max

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: For each of the n - k + 1 windows, scan its k numbers.

rows.name: Max heap with lazy delete
rows.note: Push every value. Pop stale tops at read time. It works, but the log factor is avoidable.

rows.name: Monotonic deque
rows.note: Each index is pushed once and popped at most once. The deque never holds more than k indexes.

fast.takeaway: A number that is smaller than a newer number can never be a future maximum. Throwing it away early is what makes the front always correct.

stages.title: Empty deque
stages.note: It holds indexes of numbers that could still become a maximum.

stages.title: Pop weaker from the back
stages.note: While the back is smaller or equal to the new number, pop it. It is older and weaker.

stages.title: Push the new index
stages.note: Add the new index at the back. The deque now falls from front to back.

stages.title: Expire the front
stages.note: If the front index has slid out of the window, remove it.

stages.title: Read the maximum
stages.note: Once the first window is full, the number at the front is the maximum for this window.

edges.title: Window of one
edges.why: Each window holds one number, so the answers are the numbers. The front expires and is replaced every step.

edges.title: Window is the whole array
edges.why: There is only one window. The deque ends as just the 9 and 4, with 9 in front.

edges.title: Equal values
edges.why: Pop when the back is smaller or equal. Keeping the older equal value would only expire sooner than the newer one.

edges.title: Max expires
edges.why: When the window moves past 7, it is removed from the front. The 4 takes over as the maximum.

gotchas.text: Store indexes, not values. You need the index to know when the front has slid out of the window.
Pop on less than or equal, not just less than. Otherwise equal values pile up in the deque for no reason.
Array.shift() moves every remaining element, so it is O(length) in theory. With the deque capped at k it is fine in practice. For huge k, keep a head index instead.
dq = dq[1:] is O(1) but keeps the old backing array alive. Fine for one run. In a long-lived service, copy into a fresh slice occasionally.
Do not read dq[0] or dq[len(dq)-1] on an empty slice. The loop guards with len(dq) > 0. The front read is safe because the new index was just pushed.

recap.key: Keep indexes in a deque with falling values. Pop weaker ones from the back, expire the front, and read the maximum at the front.
moves: Pop from the back while the back value is not bigger than the new one
Push the new index at the back
Pop the front if its index left the window
When the window is full, output the value at the front
